speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific location of your back pain and which leg it radiates down to, and did this start after any specific injury or activity?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: On a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate the pain intensity, and have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness in that leg? Also, does coughing or sneezing worsen the pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any weakness in your foot, such as difficulty lifting your toes or standing on your heels? Have you experienced any changes in bladder or bowel control, or numbness in the saddle area?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. No prior episodes of similar pain. Social history: Non-smoker, rarely drinks alcohol. Regular gym-goer.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify if you have any numbness or weakness in your leg, as well as any changes in bladder or bowel control, to rule out serious nerve compression. Please also specify if the pain is strictly on one side and if you have any history of kidney stones or urinary issues.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, changes in bowel or bladder function.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any numbness or weakness in your leg, and can you specify which toes are affected? I will also request an MRI of the lumbar spine to assess for a herniated disc. REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_MRI
